title: Choose methods

blocks.heading: Choose methods
blocks.text: Evaluate a method by fit to the question, evidence quality, resources and ethics. Direct observation can measure visible counts but not private reasons; interviews can ask reasons but may face recall or response bias. A researcher difficulty obstructs collection; a community problem is what the enquiry investigates.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Worked enquiry connection
blocks.text: Explain which method fits an invented enquiry about visible litter counts on safe public paths: direct structured observation or interviews asking residents to remember counts. Time and safe access are available. Observation more directly measures visible counts with consistent categories. Interviews may explore reasons but recall is weaker evidence for exact site counts; choose by the actual variable and access conditions.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect the enquiry to its actual development topic and to Population (7.1) for denominators. Keep an individual record of the real procedure, changes, findings and limits. Fictional models teach the method and must not be presented as the learner’s completed fieldwork.
